title: Regulatory Investigations and Enforcement: Responding as a Firm
summary: A ten-module programme showing firms how to prepare for, manage and respond to supervisory investigations and enforcement, from first information request to settlement.
intro: This training programme equips senior leaders, control functions and in-house lawyers to prepare for, manage and respond to supervisory investigations and enforcement action, protecting the firm, its people and its relationship with the authority.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give firms a clear, practical understanding of how authorities select, investigate and resolve enforcement cases, taught from the investigator's side so the firm can anticipate each step. Participants leave able to run a disciplined response from the first information request to settlement or decision, handle privilege, interviews and individual liability, and turn the outcome into lasting remediation.
sections.What It Covers: How enforcement cases begin, enforcement readiness, self-reporting and early engagement, information requests and formal powers, legal privilege and document preservation, compelled interviews of staff, cooperation and remediation, warning notices and settlement, individual liability and parallel proceedings, and communications and lessons learned.
Intended Audience: Chief executives, senior managers and directors who may be accountable when the firm is investigated
Heads of compliance, risk, internal audit and financial crime, and their deputies
General counsel, in-house lawyers and company secretaries who coordinate the firm's response
Learning Objectives: Explain how authorities identify, select and investigate enforcement cases, and what drives their decisions
Design an enforcement readiness framework so the firm can respond quickly and consistently to an investigation
Manage information requests, document preservation and legal privilege without creating new regulatory risk
Prepare and support staff for compelled interviews while managing conflicts between the firm and individuals
Evaluate cooperation, remediation, settlement and contest options and their effect on the outcome
Plan communications, board reporting and post-case remediation that restore the authority's confidence
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a briefing from the investigator's side with case studies, exercises and role-play, ending in a full enforcement simulation, and modules can be selected or tailored to the firm's business and risk profile.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of compliance, legal or senior management work in a regulated firm is helpful. No prior experience of enforcement proceedings is required.
Core Reading: IOSCO, Credible Deterrence in the Enforcement of Securities Regulation (2015)
IOSCO, Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation (2017)
FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)
IOSCO, Multilateral Memorandum of Understanding (MMoU) and Enhanced MMoU (2016)

modules.title: How Enforcement Cases Begin
modules.summary: How authorities use enforcement within the supervisory toolkit, where cases come from and how triage decides which matters become formal investigations, so the firm can recognise its own exposure early.
objectives: Explain the purpose of enforcement and the principle of credible deterrence
Identify the routes by which issues at the firm reach the enforcement function
Recognise the early warning signs that a supervisory matter may escalate
syllabus: Credible deterrence and where supervision ends and enforcement begins
Referral sources: supervision, whistleblowers, complaints, surveillance and other authorities
Triage criteria: seriousness, harm, evidential strength and public interest
Warning signs: escalating requests, thematic outliers and repeat findings

modules.title: Enforcement Readiness: Before the Investigation
modules.summary: The arrangements a firm should have in place before an investigation starts: a response protocol, a named team, records that can be produced, insurance and a clear route to the board.
objectives: Design an investigation response protocol with clear roles and escalation
Assess whether records, communications and data can be produced reliably
Identify insurance, indemnity and external adviser arrangements in advance
syllabus: The response playbook: team, decision rights, external counsel and board escalation
Record-keeping, communications capture and retention as enforcement evidence
Directors' and officers' insurance notifications and indemnity policies
Exercise: stress-testing the firm's readiness against a first notice

modules.title: Self-Reporting, Notification and Early Engagement
modules.summary: When and how the firm should tell the authority about a potential breach, how candour affects the outcome, and how to shape scope and timetable through early engagement.
objectives: Apply notification duties and judge when a self-report is required or advisable
Explain how openness and timely self-reporting influence enforcement outcomes
Plan early engagement with the authority on scope, timing and the firm's own review
syllabus: Notification duties, materiality and the expectation of openness
Self-reporting: timing, content and what the authority will do with it
Running an internal review alongside or ahead of the authority's investigation
Scoping meetings, case teams and agreeing a realistic timetable

modules.title: Information Requests and Formal Powers
modules.summary: How authorities use their powers to require information, documents and attendance, and how the firm responds completely, on time and without inadvertently widening the case.
objectives: Explain the information-gathering powers authorities typically hold
Manage formal requirements, deadlines and data production as a controlled project
Negotiate scope and format while preserving credibility with the case team
syllabus: Requirements for information, documents, attendance and on-site inspections
Reading a notice: scope, deadlines, format and consequences of non-compliance
Production governance: search, review, quality control and sign-off
Requests to third parties, service providers and group companies

modules.title: Legal Privilege, Confidentiality and Evidence Preservation
modules.summary: How to preserve evidence from the outset, protect legal privilege and confidentiality, and decide what to share with the authority, including internal investigation reports.
objectives: Implement legal holds and preserve documents, devices and communications
Apply legal privilege and confidentiality, and recognise how they are lost
Evaluate the risks and benefits of sharing internal reports with the authority
syllabus: Legal holds, forensic copies and chain of custody
Electronic disclosure, search terms and review workflows
Legal privilege, its limits and the risk of waiver
Sharing interview notes and reports: cooperation versus protection

modules.title: Compelled Interviews: Preparing and Supporting Staff
modules.summary: How authorities plan and conduct compelled and voluntary interviews, and how the firm prepares staff fairly, manages legal representation and conflicts, and supports wellbeing.
objectives: Explain interviewees' rights and how answers given under compulsion may be used
Prepare staff for interview without coaching or compromising the evidence
Manage representation where the interests of the firm and individuals diverge
syllabus: Compelled versus voluntary interviews: rights, cautions and use of answers
How investigators plan interviews and use documents and bundles
Firm and individual representation, conflicts and separate counsel
Role-play: preparing a senior manager for a compelled interview

modules.title: Cooperation, Remediation and Credit
modules.summary: What genuine cooperation looks like to an authority, how remediation and customer redress affect the outcome, and how to evidence that root causes have been fixed.
objectives: Explain how authorities assess cooperation, aggravating and mitigating factors
Design remediation and redress that address root causes, not symptoms
Evidence progress through independent reviews and attestations
syllabus: Cooperation in practice: openness, timeliness and no surprises
Aggravating and mitigating factors: concealment, self-reporting and remediation
Root cause analysis, redress programmes and independent expert reviews
Case study: an outcome transformed by early remediation

modules.title: Warning Notices, Representations and Settlement
modules.summary: How the authority moves from findings to decision, how the firm makes effective representations, and how to weigh settlement against contesting the case.
objectives: Analyse proposed findings against the evidence and the standard of proof
Prepare representations that are focused, evidenced and persuasive
Evaluate settlement terms, discounts and the case for contesting
syllabus: Investigation reports, warning notices and access to material
Effective representations: structure, evidence and tone
Settlement: timing, discounts, agreed facts and admissions
Penalty frameworks, contested decisions, tribunals and appeals

modules.title: Individual Liability and Parallel Proceedings
modules.summary: How investigations reach senior individuals, how the firm manages conflicts between corporate and personal interests, and how to handle criminal, civil and cross-border proceedings running in parallel.
objectives: Explain how authorities pursue individuals and what reasonable steps they expect
Manage conflicts, indemnities and separate representation for individuals
Coordinate the response across criminal, civil and multiple-authority proceedings
syllabus: Senior manager accountability, reasonable steps and prohibition orders
Conflicts of interest, indemnities and employment actions during investigations
Criminal referral, sequencing and the national FIU and other agencies
Cross-border cooperation between authorities and follow-on civil claims

modules.title: Communications, Lessons Learned and Simulation Workshop
modules.summary: Brings the programme together: managing publicity and stakeholder communications, reporting to the board, embedding lessons, and a simulation that takes a case from first notice to outcome.
objectives: Plan communications with staff, customers, investors and counterparties
Report the case and its lessons to the board with candour
Apply the programme in a full enforcement simulation
syllabus: Final notices, publicity and reputational management
Board reporting, disclosure obligations and investor communications
Post-case reviews, culture change and rebuilding the supervisory relationship
Workshop: simulation from first notice to settlement decision
